questions.question: Select the option that has used the correct tense.

options.text: Yesterday, we will be painting the door when a neighbour stops by to say hello.
Yesterday, we are painting the door when a neighbour stop by to say hello.
Yesterday, we was painting the door when a neighbour stopping by to say hello.
Yesterday, we were painting the door when a neighbour stopped by to say hello.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. Yesterday, we were painting the door when a neighbour stopped by to say hello. .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence describes an action that was ongoing in the past when another action interrupted it.
 
• The correct structure to use in such a sentence is the past continuous tense for the ongoing action and the past simple tense for the interrupting action.
 
• Therefore, "we were painting" (past continuous) and "a neighbour stopped by" (past simple) are the correct forms to use.

Correct sentence: *Yesterday, we were painting the door when a neighbour stopped by to say hello*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Past Continuous Tense:**

 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + was/were + verb(-ing).
 
• **Example:** They were having dinner when the phone rang.
 
• **Usage: **Describes an action that was happening at a specific time in the past.
 
 
 
• **Past Simple Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure: **Subject + verb (in past form).
 
• **Example: **She called him last night.
 
• **Usage: **Describes completed actions at a specific time in the past.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can replace the underlined segment in the given sentence.

No sooner had they left __their home that it started__ raining heavily.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. their home than it started .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence uses the construction "No sooner...than" which is used to indicate that one action occurred immediately after another.
 
• The correct construction is "No sooner had + subject + past participle + than + subject + past simple".
 
• In this sentence, "had they left" is correct; the corresponding part should be "than it started" to match the required structure.

Correct sentence: *No sooner had they left their home than it started raining heavily*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **No sooner...than: **

 
 
• **Structure:** No sooner + auxiliary verb (usually "had") + subject + past participle + than + subject + past simple.
 
• **Example:** No sooner had I completed the exam than the bell rang.
 
• **Usage: **Indicates that the second action happened immediately after the first action.

• **Farther:**
 
 
• **Usage:** It is primarily used to compare physical distances.
 
• **Example:** This library is farther from my home than the school.
 
 
 
• **Farthest:**

• **Example: ** Pluto is the farthest planet from the sun in our solar system.
